New graduate who is board certified or board eligible (board certification to be completed within 1 year of hire).

Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures.

cond_0171.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Laboratory Scientist II to join our team.
cond_0171.responsibilities:
Meets expectations of the applicable [Product name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Coordinates with the team to perform all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about or specific values.
Works alongside colleagues to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot laboratory instrumentation and equipment, making minor repairs as necessary or notifying Bio-med as needed.
Cross-trains to other laboratory sections as needed to support team coverage.
Helps ensure that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures.
Utilizes the Laboratory Information System.
Shares notification and documentation of critical laboratory values obtained.
Supports the processing of patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution, always cognizant of minimal pediatric specimen volumes (when required).
Participates collaboratively in the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols.
Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department.
Works with the care team to appropriately adapt assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, specific and other developmental needs of each patient served.
Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0171.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in the CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks) OR Education that has been evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS.
If certification with an expiration date is held, the certification must be maintained and kept current.
Preferred Requirements
One year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS. OR Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which must include a clinical rotation through the following sections of the laboratory: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, and Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in the [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years OR 5 years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).
New Graduate that is Board Certified or eligible (must complete Board Certification in 1 year of hire, [Location masked] excluded).

cond_0191.responsibilities:
Meets expectations of the applicable [Product name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about or specific values.
Operates, maintains, and troubleshoots laboratory instrumentation and equipment and makes minor repairs as necessary or notifies Bio-med as needed.
Must cross-train to other laboratory sections as needed.
Assures that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures.
Utilizes the Laboratory Information System.
Provides notification and documentation of critical laboratory values obtained.
Processes patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution always cognizant of minimal pediatric specimen volumes (when required).
Participates in the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols.
Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department.
Appropriately adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, specific and other developmental needs of each patient served.
Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0191.requirements:
Bachelor's degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological, or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution required; advanced degree strongly preferred. Equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks) will be considered, OR education evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological, or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
Proven track record of at least one year of demonstrated expertise for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS or other organizations approved by HHS. OR Minimum two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which must include a clinical rotation through the following sections: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids within the last 5 years. OR Substantial experience of 5 years as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS, with deep knowledge of applicable regulatory and certification standards.
If certification with an expiration date is held, the certification must be maintained and kept current.
New Graduate that is Board Certified or eligible (must complete Board Certification within 1 year of hire).

Meets expectations of the applicable [Product name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about or specific values.
Operates, maintains, and troubleshoots laboratory instrumentation and equipment and makes minor repairs as necessary or notifies Bio-med as needed.
Cross-trains to other laboratory sections as needed.
Ensures the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures.
Utilizes the Laboratory Information System.
Documents and reports critical laboratory values obtained to the appropriate party.
Processes patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution, always cognizant of minimal pediatric specimen volumes (when required).
Contributes to the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols.
Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department.
Adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, specific and other developmental needs of each patient served.
Completes all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follows all applicable policies and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0241.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution, or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks), OR education evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS.
If certification with an expiration date is held, the certification must be maintained and kept current.
Preferred Requirements
One year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS. OR Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which must include a clinical rotation through the following sections: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years. OR 5 years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).
New Graduate that is Board Certified or eligible (must complete Board Certification within 1 year of hire, [Location masked] excluded).

cond_0306.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Laboratory Scientist II to join our team.
cond_0306.responsibilities:
Meets expectations of the applicable [Product name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Coordinates with the team to perform all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about or specific values.
Works alongside Bio-med and other staff to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot laboratory instrumentation and equipment, making minor repairs as necessary or notifying Bio-med as needed.
Cross-trains to other laboratory sections as needed to support team coverage.
Helps ensure that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Collaborates to calculate, enter, and/or verify results of laboratory procedures.
Utilizes the Laboratory Information System.
Shares notification and documentation of critical laboratory values obtained.
Processes patient specimens in coordination with the team, including collection, handling, and distribution, always cognizant of minimal pediatric specimen volumes (when required).
Participates in the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols.
Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department.
Appropriately adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, specific and other developmental needs of each patient served.
Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0306.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in the CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks) OR Education that has been evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
One year of experience required for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS. OR Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which must include a clinical rotation through the following sections of the laboratory: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, and Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in the [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years OR 5 years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS.

cond_0375.requirements:

cond_0415.intro: This position performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures including specimen processing and handling, testing of patient specimens, calculating, and reporting of results, performance of quality control procedures, operation and maintenance of instruments and equipment, assisting in the development of new procedures and protocols, may perform phlebotomy and other patient-oriented tasks, and may perform other related duties as requested or directed.
cond_0415.responsibilities:
Meets expectations of the applicable [Product name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about or specific values.
Operates, maintains, and troubleshoots laboratory instrumentation and equipment and makes minor repairs as necessary or notifies Bio-med as needed.
Must cross-train to other laboratory sections as needed.
Assures that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures.
Utilizes the Laboratory Information System.
Provides notification and documentation of critical laboratory values obtained.
Processes patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution always cognizant of minimal pediatric specimen volumes (when required).
Participates in the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols.
Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department.
Appropriately adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, specific and other developmental needs of each patient served.
Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0415.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in the CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks) OR Education that has been evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS.
If certification with an expiration date is held, the certification must be maintained and kept current.
Preferred Requirements
One year of experience for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS. OR Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which must include a clinical rotation through the following sections of the laboratory: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, and Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in the [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years OR 5 years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).
New Graduate that is Board Certified or eligible (must complete Board Certification in 1 year of hire, [Location masked] excluded).
cond_0415.values: We value strong results, high standards, and the pursuit of excellent work. We believe organizations perform best when they are guided by ambition and quality.

Meets expectations of the applicable [Product name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about or specific values.
Operates, maintains, and troubleshoots laboratory instrumentation and equipment and makes minor repairs as necessary or notifies Bio-med as needed.
Must cross-train to other laboratory sections as needed.
Assures that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures.
Utilizes the Laboratory Information System.
Provides documentation of critical laboratory values obtained and notifies the appropriate party.
Processes patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution always cognizant of minimal pediatric specimen volumes (when required).
Contributes to the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols.
Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department.
Adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, specific and other developmental needs of each patient served.
Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0484.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in the CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks) OR Education that has been evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
One year of experience required for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS. OR Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which must include a clinical rotation through the following sections of the laboratory: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, and Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids in the [Location masked] or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years OR 5 years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS.

Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution, or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes [Location masked] military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks), OR education evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a [Location masked] Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.

cond_0503.requirements:

People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the kind of laboratory procedures and testing logic the work involves.
cond_0535.responsibilities:
Meets expectations of the applicable [Product name masked] Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Performs all routine and complicated laboratory procedures in the primary section to which assigned about or specific values.
Operates, maintains, and troubleshoots laboratory instrumentation and equipment and makes minor repairs as necessary or notifies Bio-med as needed.
Must cross-train to other laboratory sections as needed.
Assures that the laboratory's quality control program is properly followed.
Calculates, enters, and/or verifies results of laboratory procedures.
Utilizes the Laboratory Information System.
Provides notification and documentation of critical laboratory values obtained.
Processes patient specimens, including collection, handling, and distribution always cognizant of minimal pediatric specimen volumes (when required).
Participates in the evaluation, development, and implementation of new or updated testing procedures and protocols.
Demonstrates competence to perform assigned patient care responsibilities in a manner that meets the population-specific and developmental needs of patients served by the department.
Appropriately adapts assigned patient assessment, treatment, and/or care methods to accommodate the unique physical, psychosocial, cultural, specific and other developmental needs of each patient served.
Must complete all required compliance and regulatory tasks and follow all applicable policies and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.
cond_0535.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree or higher in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution or equivalent laboratory training and experience meeting the requirements defined in the CLIA regulation 42CFR493.1489 (includes military laboratory training courses of at least 50 weeks) OR Education that has been evaluated by an acceptable credentialing agency and deemed equivalent to a Bachelor's degree in a chemical, physical, biological or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
One year of experience required for graduates of a clinical laboratory training program approved or accredited by NAACLS, or other organizations approved by HHS. OR Two years of approved clinical laboratory experience, which must include a clinical rotation through the following sections of the laboratory: Blood Banking, Microbiology, Chemistry, and Hematology, Immunology, and Urinalysis/Body Fluids or with an accredited laboratory within the last 5 years OR 5 years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT II cannot move to a CLS II).
Must possess Certification for MT, MLS, CLS, or MLT from ASCP, AMT, AAB, or HEW/HHS.
If certification with an expiration date is held, the certification must be maintained and kept current.
New Graduate that is Board Certified or eligible (must complete Board Certification in 1 year of hire, [Location masked] excluded).
